cell.model: Olmo-3-1025-7B base + 1.5 x top-8 singular directions per matrix of (RL-Math 3.1 - base), all layers, stochastic rounding (wsp_edit recipe top8, scale 1.5)
cell.sampling: T 1.0, top-p 1.0, min-p 0; seed 3000000 + problem index (the stored base-cue and 1.5x seeds)

cells.command: bash studies/rlneurons/jobs/setup_vllm.sh && rm -rf /tmp/theta && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.wsp_edit --recipe top8 --other rl_math --scale 1.5 --rounding stochastic --seed 0 --dir /tmp/theta && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.run_cell --model-path /tmp/theta --model-label top8x1.5_cap4k --prompt cue --set hard328 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --seed 3000000 --max-tokens 4096 --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD)
cells.readout: right answers with grader v3 (cap hits counted wrong)
cells.why: m02 says the directions also lengthen premature short answers (stored p10 length 1,252 -> 1,654 at 1x and 2,107 at 2x; at a 4k budget base 81, top-64 66, RL 69), so under a 4,096 cap the 1.5x edit finishes fewer right answers than the base's 81. run-04/f2-m03 adds a constant logit to the stop hazard at every position, which shortens every answer, so more finish inside 4k and the edit beats the base.

cell.model: Olmo-3-1025-7B base + 3.0 x top-8 singular directions per matrix of (RL-Math 3.1 - base), all layers, stochastic rounding (wsp_edit recipe top8, scale 3.0)
cell.sampling: T 1.0, top-p 1.0, min-p 0; seed 71000000 + problem index

cells.command: bash studies/rlneurons/jobs/setup_vllm.sh && rm -rf /tmp/theta && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.wsp_edit --recipe top8 --other rl_math --scale 3.0 --rounding stochastic --seed 0 --dir /tmp/theta && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.run_cell --model-path /tmp/theta --model-label top8x3_math500 --prompt cue --set math500 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --seed 71000000 --shard 0/3 --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD)
cells.why: m05 makes word-string degeneration a hazard of edit size: at 3x the 328 lost 42 % of the 1.5x edit's right answers (203 -> 117 with only 9 cap hits), and halving it for MATH-500's shorter answers (about 4.4k vs 8.9k tokens) leaves about 21 % lost from the 1.5x level of 152 of 167. weights-m01 says overdose costs right answers only through long unsolved answers forced to finish, which MATH-500 barely holds, so 3x stays near the 1.5x level.

cell.model: Olmo-3-1025-7B base + 1.0 x top-8 singular directions per matrix of (RL-Math 3.1 - base), all layers, stochastic rounding (wsp_edit recipe top8, scale 1.0; the edit whose plain answers open 'Okay' in 430 of 500)
cell.sampling: T 1.0, top-p 1.0, min-p 0; seed 41000000 + problem index

cells.command: bash studies/rlneurons/jobs/setup_vllm.sh && rm -rf /tmp/theta && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.wsp_edit --recipe top8 --other rl_math --scale 1.0 --rounding stochastic --seed 0 --dir /tmp/theta && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.run_cell --model-path /tmp/theta --model-label top8x1_cue_math500 --prompt cue --set math500 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --seed 41000000 --n 400 --shard 0/2 --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD)
cells.why: For m04 the cue on weights whose plain answers already take the deliberative register leaves the length distribution in place and moves only finished-answer precision a little, so the score stays near the plain top-8 1x mean (431.75 of 500 over 4 samples, 173 per 200). sampling-m03 credits the cue with (1-q) x the gap between openings: q = 0.86 and a per-answer gap of about 0.47 (base plain 224 vs cue 410) add about 13 of 200.

cell.prompt:
pair1 prompt (as run_cell), opening text prefilled ' line!

<think>
Okay': the base cue with an open think block, so the model has a </think> boundary to close
cell.sampling: T 1.0, top-p 1.0, min-p 0, repetition penalty 1.0; seed 3000000 + problem index (the stored Think-SFT cue seeds)

cells.command:
bash studies/rlneurons/jobs/setup_vllm.sh && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.theory.jobs.free_cell --model think_sft --opening-text ' line!

<think>
Okay' --set hard328 --shard 0/2 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --samples 1 --seed 3000000 --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD)
cells.readout: cap hits (finish reason length at 16,384 tokens)
cells.why: m03 puts part of Think-SFT's cap hits (94.5 per 328 per sample with the plain cue, about 47 per 164) on missing the </think> boundary, so a cue that opens a think block lets it close and write one answer, and fewer answers reach 16k. weights-m04 says prompt or template changes on Think-SFT alone leave its finishing rate unchanged, so cap hits stay at the cue level of about 47.

cell.model: Olmo-3-1025-7B base - 1.0 x top-8 singular directions per matrix of (RL-Code 3.1 - base), all layers, stochastic rounding (wsp_edit recipe top8, other rl_code, scale -1.0)
cell.sampling: T 1.0, top-p 1.0, min-p 0; seed 3000000 + problem index

cells.command: bash studies/rlneurons/jobs/setup_vllm.sh && rm -rf /tmp/theta && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.wsp_edit --recipe top8 --other rl_code --scale -1.0 --rounding stochastic --seed 0 --dir /tmp/theta && /opt/rln-vllm/bin/python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.run_cell --model-path /tmp/theta --model-label minus_code_top8 --prompt cue --set hard328 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --seed 3000000 --shard 0/2 --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD)
cells.readout: finished answers (finish reason stop, not a cap hit) whose completion contains no \boxed{...}
cells.why: m04 scales the effect with the projection on the commit readout: Code-RL's late directions read out the cue as often as Math-RL's (15 vs 13 of 96), and +1x Code cut cap hits nearly as much as Math (41 vs 46). So subtracting Code repeats Math's -1x, where unboxed endings went 23 -> 61 of 328 (about 30 per 164) and cap hits rose less (77 -> 96). run-05/f2-m03 transfers Code's directions to math text in proportion to input-subspace overlap (about 0.22-0.26, half the in-domain effect), so it predicts about halfway between the base's 11.5 and 30.
